transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-03-05 15:00 UTC | Duration: 42m | Recording: Yes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Alex Rivera (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood CSM), Rina Gomez (Kitewell CTO), Sam Patel (Kitewell Head of MLOps), Eli Turner (Kitewell SRE), Nora Lin (Kitewell Procurement)

Summary auto-gen (may be noisy): renewal check in, eu pilot, pricing appendix, run bench, proc timeline, kms questions

Transcript body:
00:00 Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining on time, um we'll do a quick run through the plan, check-in on timelines and then alex will walk the benchmark approach.
00:10 Rina Gomez: thanks maya, appreciate it. our leadership wants us to lock the renewal for april, ideally early april, with an eu footprint live by may.
00:18 Maya Chen: copy. quick context from us — we scoped a modest uplift in q4 and you asked about adding an eu private pilot plus 24/7 sla for checkout flows. is that still accurate?
00:28 Sam Patel: yes that's right. main drivers: 1) latency for eu users is popping at peak, 2) regulatory requests from our EU customers about data residency and key control.
00:38 Alex Rivera: got it. so two things we usually recommend: initial dedicated capacity in eu-west with private VPC peering for data-in-place, or a private on-prem pilot if you need air-gapped. both support KMS, but the integration path differs.
00:52 Eli Turner: quick Q — does the dedicated option let us use our KMS (we have a vault cluster) or we need to use Redwood-managed keys?
01:00 Alex Rivera: you can bring-your-own-KMS for Dedicated and Private. for hosted it's Redwood KMS by default, but we do offer customer-managed keys with an add-on and stricter attestation. sometimes the name's mis-read in docs as KMS/HSM but that's what we mean.
01:15 Sam Patel: sounds good. also curious on fallbacks — if the eu cluster saturates, we don't want checkout latency to spike; what's the failover behavior?
01:25 Priya Nair: we typically configure smart routing with region fallback to a lower-cost host in us-east or another compatible variant. we can set an aggressive canary so only non-critical traffic crosses until you trust the eu nodes.
01:37 Rina Gomez: that trade-off is fine but we need to quantify expected p95 delta. ie, if eu fails over to us-east, how much added RTT?
01:45 Alex Rivera: ballpark the additional RTT would be 120-180ms for eu -> us-east depending on network. you can trim cost by using quantized model variants; that will impact quality a bit. we can model it in the benchmark.
01:59 Maya Chen: on pricing — we'll send an updated appendix with eu SKUs and reserved capacity tiers. given your prior usage we sketched Tier B uplift (roughly 2.5x current tokens/day) for the first 3 months then migrate to steady state.
02:12 Nora Lin: procurement question — if we sign an amendment for a start date of Apr 15, when will invoices kick and how does proration work?
02:20 Maya Chen: invoices align to the amendment start; proration is pro-rata for that month. i'll include the payment schedule in the appendix.
02:28 Sam Patel: benchmark details — alex, can you run a throughput run that includes cold-starts and kv cache warm paths? those are where we see most variance.
02:36 Alex Rivera: absolutely. plan is: 1) CPU cold-start path, 2) warm KV cache topologies, 3) long-sequence chat loads, 4) p95 tail probing. we'll capture token/sec and cost-per-1M tokens. i'll share the test plan and result template.
02:50 Rina Gomez: about security docs, we need SOC2 scope, ISO certs and network architecture diagram showing vpc peering and subnet flow. also audit log retention details.
02:59 Priya Nair: we'll share SOC2 + ISO artifacts and a KMS integration guide. audit logs retention can be extended as an enterprise add-on; default is 90 days but we can extend to 365 for the package.
03:13 Eli Turner: one more — do you have latency SLOs you commit to for Dedicated vs Private?
03:18 Maya Chen: Dedicated has SLA-backed throughput/uptime but latency SLOs are a function of model choice and instance types. for Private, you control the infra latency; Redwood will guarantee orchestration availability. we'll annotate expected p95s in the appendix per model.
03:33 Rina Gomez: competitor question — CloudGiant AI offered us a cheaper per-token but no KV cache persistence, and atlas compute said they'd do eu-hosted but no customer KMS. that influenced our leaning here.
03:45 Maya Chen: noted. our differentiator is the unified routing and KV caching which helps cut per-token cost on conversational flows.
03:52 Sam Patel: ok next steps — run benchmarks, send contract amendment, security docs, confirm procurement dates.
03:59 Maya Chen: yep. alex — we'll need the benchmark in time to review before your procurement sign date. can you commit to dropping results by 2025-03-12?
04:08 Alex Rivera: yes, i can run the tests and share a results deck by the 12th. i'll include both p95 and cost curves, and a scenario with quantized variants.
04:18 Nora Lin: procurement timeline: we need signed amendment by Mar 25 to get finance to cut PO before end of march. so that April 15 start is tight but possible.
04:28 Maya Chen: understood, we'll accelerate the appendix. Sam, anything else from your side on the technical acceptance criteria?
04:35 Sam Patel: just that the p95 for checkout needs to be under 200ms in eu on steady state; otherwise we'll ask for additional reserved throughput or local edge caching.
04:46 Maya Chen: we'll call that out. if benchmark shows >200ms we'll propose one of two mitigations: add reserved nodes in the eu cluster or enable prefix/KV caching aggressively which reduces token compute.
04:58 Rina Gomez: final ask — can you send a suggested rollback plan? in case the eu pilot has issues, we need steps to revert traffic.
05:06 Priya Nair: yes, we'll include an A/B rollback playbook with traffic weighting and circuit-breaker thresholds.
05:14 Maya Chen: perfect. recap of next steps and owners (sending appendix, bench, security docs, procurement confirm). thanks all, we'll meet same time next week to review the bench.
05:28 Rina Gomez: thanks everyone.
05:31 Meeting ends.
